discovery: Squeezed states of light and quantum-enhanced precision measurement beyond the standard quantum limit
motivation: Caves showed in 1981 that quantum noise in interferometers originates in vacuum fluctuations entering the unused port, and that injecting squeezed vacuum could beat the standard quantum limit. Kimble's group realised this programme experimentally, generating strongly squeezed light by parametric down-conversion and demonstrating sub-shot-noise interferometric measurement, establishing squeezed light as a practical quantum resource. Schnabel pioneered high-degree, low-frequency squeezing sources and their first long-term operation in a gravitational-wave observatory, GEO600. Since 2019 squeezed light has run routinely in LIGO and Virgo, raising detection rates by tens of percent, and frequency-dependent squeezing now beats quantum noise across the whole band. This is the first time engineered quantum states have improved a large scientific instrument, and the work founded quantum metrology, now central to atomic clocks, magnetometry and quantum sensing. Together these contributions expanded what humanity can measure.
